title: Radiomic models distinguish pathology-defined pancreatic cyst risk in surgical cohorts
summary: Learned CT-radiomic scores combined with a conventional imaging feature distinguished source-defined benign and malignant pancreatic cyst groups in surgical cohorts. Models developed using 262 patients were evaluated in two 50-patient test sets and a separately recruited 34-patient cohort. The result is retrospective pathology-reference diagnostic evaluation, not evidence that the models improve screening or decisions about surgery.
ai_technology: LASSO feature selection; multiple learned radiomic classifiers; clinical-radiomic regression
organization: Peking Union Medical College Hospital; Guangzhou Medical University; Chengdu First People’s Hospital

evidence.tested: Eleven radiomic classifiers were trained in 262 patients, assessed in 50 temporal internal and 50 external cases, and combined with solid-component information. A34-patient prospectively recruited cohort was subsequently analyzed with those models.
evidence.unknown: All included patients underwent surgery, restricting the disease spectrum and reference availability. Prospective recruitment does not establish that a frozen model was evaluated before outcomes; validation is classified as retrospective. Full preprocessing/feature-selection nesting is not completely specified. The source-defined grouping combines different lesion types/grades and is not a universal management threshold. Separate fluid-omics mechanism claims are outside this record.
evidence.ai_role: Learned classifiers map selected CT image features to pathology-defined cyst labels; resulting radiomic scores add information to a clinical imaging-feature model evaluated in separate patient datasets.

source_review.scope: Exact primary XML front DOI/title/PMCID/date; clinical cohorts, pathology-label definitions, radiomic/statistical model and validation Methods/Results. Raw biological assay protocols and mechanistic omics sections not processed. Same-day primary bibliographic/notice snapshot reused.
